{{Quote|This station is now the ultimate power in the universe. I suggest we use it.|[[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Conan Antonio Motti/Legends|Motti]]|<ref name="ANH" />}}
The '''DS-1 Orbital Battle Station''', or '''mk. 1 deep-space mobile battlestation''' better known as the '''Death Star''' or '''Death Star I''', and known to the public as the '''Imperial Planetary Ore Extractor''', was a massive [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Battle station/Legends|battle station]] and [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapon]] with a diameter of 120 kilometers designed to enforce law and order throughout the Empire with the threat of [[Planet/Legends|planetary]] destruction.<ref name="TEGTW" /> It started off as the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatist]] '''Ultimate Weapon''' before becoming the '''Expeditionary Battle Planetoid Development Initiative''' or '''Project Death Star''' after it ceased to be a Separatist project and became an Imperial one in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]].

Its design origins lay in the [[Raith Sienar/Legends|Raith Sienar's]] [[Expeditionary Battle Planetoid]]. Sienar, who had become disillusioned about the project due to its impracticalities, nonetheless shared the design with [[Wilhuff Tarkin/Legends|Wilhuff Tarkin]] in [[29 BBY/Legends|29 BBY]]. Tarkin, claiming the design as his own, shared Sienar's ideas with [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]]. Palpatine ordered [[Bevel Lemelisk]] and [[Tol Sivron]] to work with [[Poggle the Lesser/Legends|Poggle the Lesser's]] [[Geonosian hive/Legends|Geonosian hives]] on the design. During the [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|First Battle of Geonosis]], Palpatine's secret apprentice, [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]], brought the improved design back to Palpatine.

Around [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], near the end of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], construction of the first Death Star had begun at occupied [[Geonosis/Legends|Geonosis]], and construction continued after the rise of the Galactic Empire. Under the Empire, the projects headquarters moved mulitple times from Geonosis to [[Seswenna/Legends|Seswenna]] and then to the [[Patriim system/Legends|Patriim system]].<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> In [[3 BBY/Legends|3 BBY]],<ref name="3 BBY">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' states that the [[Death Star prototype]]'s successfull test occured after [[3 BBY/Legends|3 BBY]]. As ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' states that the Death Star project was moved to the [[Horuz system/Legends|Horuz system]] after the protype's successfull test firing, and ''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' establishes that the Death Star Was being constructed in the Horuz system in 3 BBY, the Death Star must have moved to the Horuz system in 3 BBY</ref> the project was moved to its final location, the [[Horuz system/Legends|Horuz system]].

==Description==
{{Quote|Look at the size of that thing!|[[Wedge Antilles/Legends|Wedge Antilles]]|audio=LookAtTheSizeOfThatThing.flac|<ref name="ANH" />}}
[[File:DeathStarIDiagram-EGVV.jpg|thumb|left|180px|[[:Category:Technical drawing images|Schematics]] of the first Death Star]]

===Design===
The DS-1 Orbital Battle Station,<ref name="RECG">''[[Rebellion Era Campaign Guide]]''</ref> or mk. 1 deep-space mobile battlestation<ref name="CV">[[Star Wars: Complete Vehicles (2013)|''Star Wars: Complete Vehicles'']]</ref> better known as the Death Star or Death Star I, and known to the public as the Imperial Planetary Ore Extractor,<ref name="XWing Wedge's Gamble">''[[X-Wing: Wedge's Gamble]]''</ref> was a massive battlestation built for planetary destruction. The basic structure of the station was a sphere the size of a Class-IV [[Moon/Legends|moon]],<ref name="DSn" /> with a kilometer-wide trench containing docking bays running around its equator. It was the very incarnation of the [[Tarkin Doctrine/Legends|Tarkin Doctrine]]. Because of its size and shape, it was sometimes mistaken for a small moon.<ref name="ANH" />

The first Death Star, like its successor, was divided into two hemispheres, each subdivided into 12 bridge-controlled zones, for a total of twenty four zones<ref name="SWTJ" /> also known as sprawls or sectors. Each sprawl would have [[Food_synthesizer/Legends|food replicators]], [[hangar]] bays, hydroponics, detention blocks, medical centers, armories, command centers, and every other facility needed to provide service for any mission deemed necessary. In an emergency, auxiliary command centers located in each sprawl provided full weapons and maneuverability control, for a redundancy depth of twice a dozen.<ref name="DSn" /> Each zone had its own bridge, and each zone bridge reported to the Death Star's overbridge, located just above the superlaser.<ref name="TEGTW" /> The Death Star comprised eighty-four separate internal levels, which where 1,148 meters (4,685 feet) in height. Each level had 357 4 meter (13.1 foot) high sublevels.<ref name="CV" /> A nominal number of sub-levels were then to be stacked around the surface of the sphere, encompassing the inner stacked levels. A number of the Death Star's docking bays were reserved as executive docking bays for high-ranking personnel, featuring larger facilities and more significant defenses.

The battlestation had two massive [[Sublight engine/Legends|sublight engines]] in the midsection and a formidable [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]] system. Driven by 123 individual generators tied to one navigational matrix, the Class 4 hyperdrive was fast enough to allow the Death Star to travel thousands of [[Light-year/Legends|light-years]] from [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]] to [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin IV]] in only a few hours. All engineers working near the highly radioactive engines wore radiation suits to minimize harmful exposure.<ref name="SWTJ" /> [[Grand Moff/Legends|Grand Moff]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin/Legends|Wilhuff Tarkin]] once likened walking inside the Death Star to walking inside the [[Caves of Corips]], but with illuminated tubing and plastisteel replacing the natural surroundings.<ref name="DSTC" />

===Locations and facilies===
<div style="float: right">[[File:Superlaser2.jpg|thumb|180px|The Death Star's [[Superlaser/Legends|superlaser]] fires on [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]]]]</div>
Facilities included parks, shops, and other amenities for the [[Human/Legends|Human]] crew, as well as numerous infrastructure necessities such as trash compactors. The [[Hull/Legends|hull]] of the planetoid was covered in [[Quadanium steel/Legends|quadanium steel]].<ref name="DSn" />

Near the northern pole, a [[Emperor's throne room|hundred-meter tower]] was constructed and shielded to near impenetrability for the [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] to use as personal quarters while on board. Operational command of the space station took place from the [[Overbridge (Death Star I)/Legends|overbridge]], which included the [[Death Star conference room/Legends|conference room]]. A high-speed shuttle system was reserved for officers to traverse the station quickly.

===Design flaw===
[[File:DeathStarElevationPlan-DeathStarOwnersTechnicalManual.jpg|thumb|left|Elevation [[:Category:Technical drawing images|plans]] for the first Death Star]]
The Death Star's design included a small but significant flaw: an exposed [[Thermal exhaust port/Legends|thermal exhaust port]]. At one point in the construction process, this exhaust port was identified as unnecessary. When [[Teela Kaarz|the architect]] responsible for the area asked the Wookiee overseeing construction of the area to omit the port, he insisted on getting the amendment to the plans in writing. Before the architect had a chance to submit such an amendment, the Wookiee became ill and was confined to a medcenter, and his replacement built the port as specified in the plans. The port was two meters wide, approximately the size of a womp rat; lay at the end of a large [[Meridian trench/Legends|trench]] in the hull of the battle station; and was [[Ray shield/Legends|ray shielded]] against energy weapons such as [[Laser cannon/Legends|laser cannons]].<ref name="DSn" />

===Armaments and defensive systems===
{{Quote|Once completed it will measure a hundred and twenty kilometers in diameter, will have a complement of twenty-seven thousand and forty-eight officers, seven hundred seventy-six thousand, five hundred seventy-six troops, pilots, and other combat personnel, along with an additional four hundred thousand support personnel and twenty-five thousand stormtroopers. Besides the necessary crew, the Death Star will carry assault shuttles, blast boats, strike cruisers, drop ships, land vehicles, and more than seven thousand TIE fighters. Its hull will be protected by ten thousand turbolaser batteries, two thousand five hundred laser cannons, and more than seven hundred tractor-beam projectors.''"<br />"''No offense, but how could you possibly know these things?''"<br />"''We know because beings sacrificed their lives to find out.|[[Kyle Katarn]] and [[Mon Mothma/Legends|Mon Mothma]] while learning about the Death Star|<ref name="Dark Forces: Soldier for the Empire">''[[Dark Forces: Soldier for the Empire]]''</ref>}}
===The superlaser===
{{Quote|Several wings of TIE fighters suddenly decided to leave the station, more than a thousand ships, and shortly thereafter you might recall that the lights dimmed for a couple of seconds? My guess is the power capacitors that fill up a big chunk of this big metal ball got diverted to that big honkin’ gun.|Rodo to Memah Roothes|<ref name="DSn" />}}
As impressive as the Death Star's design was, its armament and defensive measures were also extensive. Its primary weapon was its [[Concave Dish Composite Beam Superlaser]], which Bevel Lemelisk had included in the final design. Although Tarkin had initially intended for the Death Star's weapon to "rock a [targeted] world to its very core," the final superlaser design was capable of shattering worlds, leaving behind only asteroid ruins. There were also plans for installing a composite beam superlaser as an alternative due to the challenges of building an operational, single-beam [[Superlaser/Legends|superlaser]], which required a mechanical arm to move it into place, although the plans were scrapped when the engineers resolved the technical difficulties of the planet-shattering superlaser.

The entirety of the Death Star's spherical design, including the majority of its interior volume, was dedicated to the support and maintenance of the superlaser. The diameter of the superlaser cannon well was approximately 35 kilometers. The energy for the superweapon originated from deep within the battle station, and was channeled into an array of eight initiator laser cannons. The eight laser cannons, via tributary beams, then converged into a central nexus point above the cannon well to form a powerful single beam. The superlaser likewise required eight [[superlaser firing station]]s: four primary stations plus four backups in case one of the stations failed. The superlaser was dangerous even to itself, so various safeguards were implemented to prevent the battlestation from being consumed by its own power, with several being resolved via Project Hammertong. One of these were the tributary beam shafts, with eight lining the circumference of the superlaser weapon. The tributary beam shafts, originally meant for Hammertong, were constructed at Desolation Station. Focusing coils also lined the tributary shafts to maintain the beams' integrity. The tributary beams had to be perfectly calibrated and aligned; otherwise, the central beam would misfocus and dissipate, resulting in a flurry of backscatter that could severely damage or even destroy the superlaser housing. The firing process generated magnetic fields and gravitational flux, necessitating their dissipation to prevent the amplification crystals from becoming misaligned and the battle station from tearing apart.

The northern hemisphere held the main armament of the station, a fearsome [[Concave Dish Composite Beam Superlaser|superlaser]]. This weapon had the external appearance of a bowl many kilometers wide. When activated, eight separate beams were each activated by a crystal through the [[Tributary beam|particle accelerator tubes]], amplified through rings, and conjoined to form one of eight separate beams that would converge outside the dish, focusing into a point to form a single incredibly powerful superlaser beam. The power settings of the superlaser were adjustable, allowing for the destruction of naval vessels and planets alike. Blasts with the power to destroy naval vessels could be fired roughly once every minute, while planet-destroying blasts could only be fired once per day.<ref name="SWTJ">''[[Star Wars Technical Journal]]''</ref> This [[Superlaser/Legends|superlaser]] was powerful enough to destroy even a shielded planet with a single shot.

At full power, the superlaser required a standard day (24 hours) to recharge,<ref name="TEGTW" /> while usage of the superlaser against spaceborne vessels only required a minute of recharging.

===Other weaponry and features===
A downside to the presence of the superlaser was that the Death Star had to forgo all but the most rudimentary shielding capabilities in order to achieve such destructive power. However, its surface-to-air defenses were sufficient to make up for its lack of efficient shielding. It possessed 5,000 [[Taim & Bak/Legends|Taim & Bak]] [[XX-9 heavy turbolaser/Legends|XX-9 heavy turbolasers]], 2,500 [[Borstel Galactic Defense/Legends|Borstel Galactic Defense]] [[MS-1 ion cannon/Legends|MS-1 ion cannons]], 2,500 Borstel Galactic Defense [[SB-920 laser cannon]]s, and 5,000 Taim & Bak [[D6 turbolaser]] batteries that acted as its surface-to-air defenses. The SB-920 batteries were largely congregated around the Death Star's trenches, were powerful enough to destroy starfighters with a single shot, and utilized an advanced Target Acquisition and Targeting (TAT) system similar to that of certain Imperial surface-to-air defense systems. The XX-9 heavy turbolasers used on the Death Star were variants that had four sections and were overall larger. To ensure the turrets didn't cause friendly fire and to deter hijackers from attacking their posts, a safety mechanism automatically locked them up when any part of the Death Star was within their sights, making them disadvantageous against starfighters. Besides defense, the turbolaser batteries acted as directional markers for TIE fighter pilots.

Shield-projection towers on the Death Star's surface emitted energy fields that covered the Death Star's city sprawls, protecting them from space debris as well as providing limited defense against energy weapons, due to most of the Death Star's energy reserves being harnessed for the superlaser. At least three shield-projection towers were necessary for a city sprawl, with their power cells, machinery, and shield-operator stations located at the bases of the towers. In addition, they were highly concentrated around the tower containing the Emperor's throne room, for obvious reasons. Shield operation fell under the jurisdiction of [[Battle Station Operations/Legends|Battle Station Operations]], with various officers, operators, and technicians tasked with manning the shield-projection towers' stations to ensure that the shields were always in full working order. During battle, the shields of neighboring sprawls could overlap to create a continuous blanket of energy over the surface.

The battlestation also had field generators, which included a jamming field that affected every sensor of enemy ships except sight, and could create distortion potent enough to reduce the maneuverability of starfighters to less than point three, at least along the [[Meridian trench/Legends|meridian trench]] housing the [[Thermal exhaust port/Legends|thermal exhaust port]].<ref name="ANH novelization">[[Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)|''Star Wars'' Episode IV: ''A New Hope'' novelization]]</ref>

The Death Star's hull plating was made of military-grade Quadanium steel, most of which had been drawn and processed from asteroidal metal. Because of the challenges of not only creating the material necessary, but also producing enough to install the plating onto the station, several sections of the Death Star were pressurized during the installation of the hull for efficiency purposes, such as storage space for supplies during construction as well as temporary habitats for laborers. The Death Star's hull from a distance appeared relatively smooth to the naked eye.

The Death Star had 768 modified Phylon Q7 tractor beam projectors, of which 24 were assigned for each zone of the Death Star. The projectors in each zone could concentrate one or all of their tractor beams onto a single target from a significant enough distance to ensnare distant enemy ships in a virtually unbreakable energy bubble, and were powerful enough to capture the vessels long before the vessels' sensors could identify it as a battle station instead of a small moon. Each required a crew of ten to operate, and was coupled to the main reactor to prevent accidents caused by generator malfunctions. There were seven power coupling terminals in all, identified atop a 35-kilometer-tall generator tower, and providing energy for more than 700 tractor beams. However, disabling even one of the coupling sites from the main reactor would result in the tractor beam becoming inoperative.

Aside from the outer defenses and armaments on the surface of the station, the inner areas of the station also provided a significant amount of security measures as well, including [[metallic spikes]]<ref name="SW1991">[[Star Wars (1991 video game)|''Star Wars'' video game (1991)]]</ref> (which were directly inspired by the stalagmite-filled pits within the various cavern networks on Tatooine<ref name="SWHB">''[[Star Wars Hint Book]]''</ref>), BlasTech Class VI automated laser projectors, which were linked by security cameras, and IT-O interrogator droids, which sometimes acted as defensive systems against intruders.<ref name="SW:RSIII:RS">''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron III: Rebel Strike]]''</ref>

The Death Star possessed a complement of 11,000 combat vehicles, 7,000 TIE fighters, four strike [[Cruiser/Legends|cruisers]] and more than 20,000 other military and [[Transport/Legends|transport]] vehicles.<ref name="TEGTW" />

Overall, the Death Star's firepower had more destructive firepower than half of the Imperial Navy,<ref name="TCSWE">{{CSWECite|Death Star, Death Star II|I|176}}</ref> and was regared as the most powerful force in the galaxy.<ref name="DSn" />

===Command structure===
Owing to the rigid command structure of various Imperial organizations, the Death Star's command structure, known as command sectors, was just as rigid.<ref name="DSOTM" />

The battle station was under the direct command of [[Grand Moff/Legends|Grand Moff]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin/Legends|Wilhuff Tarkin]]. Below him was a triumvirate composed of [[Army Command]], [[Naval Command (Imperial)|Naval Command]], and [[Battle Station Command/Legends|Battle Station Command]], represented by [[High General]] [[Cassio Tagge/Legends|Cassio Tagge]], [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Conan Antonio Motti/Legends|Conan Antonio Motti]], and [[General/Legends|General]] [[Hurst Romodi/Legends|Hurst Romodi]], respectively, although when the [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Galactic Emperor]] made visits, his authority superseded theirs. Below them were the Operations Chiefs for the Army, Navy and Battle Station Operations, all of whom were held by officers with the rank of [[Colonel/Legends|colonel]]. Below each Operations Chief, there were eight [[Major/Legends|majors]], each representing specific departments under their branch of operations, alongside four majors tasked with the general, service, technical, security, and military sectors (the last including [[Imperial Army trooper/Legends|Army troopers]], the [[Death Star Trooper/Legends|Death Star troopers]] [a subset of the [[Imperial Navy Trooper/Legends|Imperial Navy troopers]]], [[Imperial gunner/Legends|gunners]], and [[TIE pilot]]s). Lastly, [[Lieutenant/Legends|lieutenants]] were tasked with supervising the command sectors and were the lowest-ranked officers to do so, relegated to [[Command sector duty post]]s.<ref name="DSOTM" />

The only exceptions to the command structure were members of the [[Stormtrooper Corps/Legends|Stormtrooper Corps]], and the Emperor's emissary, [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]], the latter of whom answered to Grand Moff Tarkin alone. Members of the Army and Navy portions of the Death Star could call upon the stormtroopers' services if necessary, although with the firm understanding that they fell under neither jurisdiction and were to obey the Emperor alone.<ref name="DSOTM" />

==History==
===Creation of the "Battle Planetoid" concept===
The concept for the Death Star could be found in its precursor, the "[[Expeditionary Battle Planetoid]]." [[Raith Sienar/Legends|Raith Sienar]] came up with the concept by [[29 BBY/Legends|29 BBY]], around the time of the [[Second Battle of Zonama Sekot]]. Sienar made concept designs of the Battle Planetoid, an immense space station<ref name="TERC" /> with a 100 km diameter main sphere and two smaller spheres.<ref name="DSn" /> The design would require massive advanced in hypermatter technology, and Sienar envisioned the station being powered by ice asteroids.<ref name="TEA" />

Raith showed the designs to the commander of the [[Outland Regions Security Force/Legends|Republic Outland Regions Security Force]], Wilhuff Tarkin.<ref name="TERC" /> Tarkin was interested in the concept, as it allowed to break the "[[stateless strategy]]" of warfare.<ref name="TEGTW" /> However, by the time Sienar showed the design to Tarkin, Sienar had already lost interest in the design,<ref name="TEA" /> thinking it impractical<ref name="TEGTW" /> due to the technological advances required for its completion. However, Tarkin, who esteemed the design more than Sienar, showed the design to [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], claiming it as his own as part of the [[Tarkin Doctrine/Legends|Tarkin Doctrine]].<ref name="TEA" />

===Separatist beginnings===
{{Quote|&laquo;The Jedi must not find our designs for the Ultimate Weapon. If they find out what we are planning to build, we're doomed.&raquo;''"<br />"''I will take the designs with me to Coruscant. They will be much safer there&hellip;with my master.|[[Archduke/Legends|Archduke]] [[Poggle the Lesser/Legends|Poggle the Lesser]] and [[Count of Serenno/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]] on Geonosis|<ref name="AOTC" />}}
[[File:UltimateWeaponPlans-AOTC.png|thumb|right|200px|The plans for the Ultimate Weapon given to [[Count/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]] by [[Poggle the Lesser/Legends|Poggle the Lesser]] during the [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|Battle of Geonosis]]]]
Palpatine then ordered [[Bevel Lemelisk]] and [[Tol Sivron]] to work with [[Poggle the Lesser/Legends|Poggle the Lesser]] and his [[Geonosian hive/Legends|Geonosian hives]] to pusue the needed advance in hypermatter technology,<ref name="TEGTW" /> as well as structural concerns. Months prior to the Clone Wars, a sizable grant from [[Sienar Fleet Systems/Legends|Sienar Systems]] was provided to the [[Ministry of Science (Galactic Republic)/Legends|Republic Ministry of Science]], allowing engineers and scientists such as [[Paldis Doxin]], [[Nasdra Magrody]], and [[Umak Leth]] to continue research into translational hypermatter energy applications and solutions.<ref>{{HoloNetNewsWeb|50|business/1344_2.html|Ministry of Science Continues Hypermatter Studies}}</ref><ref>{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/hnn/001.html#rss|text=HoloNet News &mdash; A Galaxy Divided}}</ref> When [[Geonosis/Legends|Geonosis]] seceded from the Republic, Lemelisk was concered about the project. Palpatine, however, remained oddly unconcerned, and assured Lemelisk that the Separatists would never put the weapon into production.<ref name="TEA" />

In [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]],<ref name="NEC" /> [[Poggle the Lesser/Legends|Poggle the Lesser]], leader of the Geonosians, returned the top-secret design to [[Count/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]] to prevent it from falling into the hands of the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] during the [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|Battle of Geonosis]]. Dooku took the designs back to [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] and gave them to [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]], his [[Sith Master/Legends|Sith Master]].<ref name="AOTC" /> These plans would later be fused with Wilhuff Tarkin and [[Raith Sienar/Legends|Raith Sienar's]] vision<ref name="DSn" /> of an [[Expeditionary Battle Planetoid]].<ref name="RP">''[[Rogue Planet]]''</ref>

Near the end of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]],<ref name="TEA" /> Sidious ordered Geonosian builders to begin construction on the station over their<ref name="ROTS:VD" /> occupied<ref name="TEA" /> homeworld. Hundreds of thousands of workers were busy building the station throughout the war.<ref name="ROTS:VD" /> Around five months after the Battle of Geonosis, Dooku briefly considered halting production of the Weapon in favor of the [[Planet Killer]], but changed his mind after the demonstration failed, thanks to sabotage by [[Mace Windu/Legends|Mace Windu]].<ref name="RMR">{{CWACite|2|Run Mace Run}}</ref> 17 months after the start of the war, Geonosian technicians on [[Zaadja/Legends|Zaadja]] were observed working on the Weapon's design.<ref name="R67">[[Republic 67|''Republic'' 67]]</ref>

In [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] Palpatine sent the [[501st Legion/Legends|501st Legion]] on a mission to [[Mygeeto/Legends|Mygeeto]] where they were to collect an [[Energy crystal|energy sample]] that would be used in the station's superlaser of the soon to be [[Declaration of a New Order|formed]] [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]].<ref name="BFII" /> During the last few weeks of the war, the [[Separatist Council/Legends|Separatist Council]] debated on ways to prolong the war, to allow their secret weapon time to be finished.<ref name="EA:ROF">''[[Reversal of Fortune]]''</ref>

===Imperial construction===
{{Quote|I guess this explains what the Empire wants with all those Wookiee slaves, droids alone couldn't build that monster. Not in a thousand years. Nor could the scum you'd usually find in an Imperial prison.|Galen Marek, upon seeing the Death Star for the first time|<ref name="The Force Unleashed (novel)">[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed (novelization)|''Star Wars: The Force Unleashed'' novelization]]</ref>}}
[[File:Construction_of_the_Death_Star.png|thumb|left|250px|[[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] and [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] witness the construction of the first Death Star.]]
Following the [[Mission to Mustafar/Legends|deaths]] of all the members of the Separatist Council, and the end of the Clone Wars in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], a majority of the Separatist holdings were turned over to the newly established Galactic Empire, including the unfinished battlestation.<ref name="ROTS">{{Film|III}}</ref> Wilhuff Tarkin was appointed to mastermind the secret development project. Tarkin's creative work and thought had resulted in the realization of the Death Star as the Empire's ultimate weapon.

To help build the superweapon and curry the Emperor's favor, Tarkin had Darth Vader lead an Imperial [[Battle of Kashyyyk (19 BBY)|invasion of Kashyyyk]], where they enslaved [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiees]] for labor.<ref name="DL:TRODV">''[[Dark Lord: The Rise of Darth Vader]]''</ref> These Wookiees were transported to the Death Star's construction site. Much of the needed funding came from appropriated funds originally earmarked for the [[Department of System Exploration]] and the [[Department of Public Works]].

However, despite these early advances in labor and funding, the project nearly ended before it began. Although much of the technology of the Death Star was impressive, actually building it proved to be more difficult than anyone imagined. The project dragged out over nineteen years as labor union disputes along with the supply and design problems slowed the construction. Efforts were not helped by repeated&mdash;albeit usually unsuccessful&mdash;sabotage efforts. In addition, Lemelisk had to undergo Bacta treatment after being Force-choked by Darth Vader, requiring a [[Unidentified Death Star architect|temporary replacement]] to oversee the development.<ref name="DSD" /> Actual effective work on the station took less than two years, and involved resources from every corner of the Empire being funneled to complete the project.<ref name="SWTJ" />

Of particular concern was the technology required to create the massive superlaser, the heart of the weapon. To this end,<ref name="NEC" /> Tarkin brought together some of the most brilliant minds of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] (including [[Tol Sivron]], [[Qwi Xux]], and [[Bevel Lemelisk]]) to build a proof-of-concept model at [[Maw Installation]]. This model would eventually become known as the [[Death Star prototype]].<ref name="JS">''[[Jedi Search]]''</ref>

[[Tag Rogaren]] has been appointed chief weapons systems engineer. He conceived and built the superlaser array of that battle station.<ref name="SW09"/>

Besides the concave dish model of the battle station's superlaser, other superweapon systems proposed during its development included a [[Resonance projector|Resonance Torpedo Launcher]] system, an [[Interplanetary Ion Cannon]], and a regular [[Composite Beam Superlaser]] model.<ref name="DSD" />

[[File:DS1_under_construction.jpg|thumb|right|200px|The Death Star under construction]]
It is uncertain exactly when the term "Death Star" came into use in connection with the project. The earliest known reference to the name Death Star as a codename for the project was in a memorandum c. [[5 BBY/Legends|5 BBY]] written by Imperial [[Advisor/Legends|advisor]] [[Ars Dangor/Legends|Ars Dangor]], which formally placed [[Wilhuff Tarkin/Legends|Wilhuff Tarkin]] in overall command of the project. Once the [[Imperial Ministry of Propaganda]] began using the name Death Star, the name stuck.

Even before the Death Star became fully operational, its detention blocks began to fill with detainees. Political troublemakers, [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] insurgents (who were beginning to organize), dangerous pirate forces, and even some survivors of the [[Royal Naboo Security Forces/Legends|Royal Naboo Security Forces]] who had boldly tried to stop their [[Battle of Naboo (Imperial Period)|Queen's assassination]], as well as myriad other enemies of the Empire, were made to quietly "disappear" from public view within the enormous prisons of the incomplete battle station.

In the year [[2 BBY/Legends|2 BBY]], four individuals who would later become leaders of the Rebel Alliance were transferred to the Death Star: the Senators [[Bail Prestor Organa/Legends|Bail Organa]], [[Garm Bel Iblis/Legends|Garm Bel Iblis]], and [[Mon Mothma/Legends|Mon Mothma]], along with a former [[Jedi General/Legends|Jedi General]] named [[Rahm Kota/Legends|Rahm Kota]]. Palpatine had the four sent to the battle station following their capture on [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]], planning to have them interrogated and tortured, followed by public execution. This plan was [[Battle on Death Star I|foiled]] by the former apprentice of Darth Vader, [[Galen Marek]]. Galen arrived and attempted to rescue the rebels, and in the end apparently sacrificed himself so the four leaders could escape.<ref name="SWTFU">''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed]]''</ref> Further, albeit limited, information about the Death Star's development was intercepted by the [[Bothan Spynet/Legends|Bothan Spynet]] and made its way to the Rebel Alliance via low-security communiqu&eacute;s, something that Lemelisk had anticipated.<ref name="Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide" />

At some point afterwards, the Death Star's reconstruction was reassigned to Geonosis. During this time, it was also heavily guarded by the Imperials. A ''StarSpeeder 1000'' that had escaped from an Imperial [[Raid at Spaceport THX1138|raid at the Star Tours space station]] and was delivering a [[Unidentified Rebel spy|Rebel agent]] to the Rebel Fleet ended up being attacked by Darth Vader's fighter squadrons as well as the Mandalorian bounty hunter [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]]. This eventually culminated in a fight in the inner workings of the Death Star, which suffered minor damage.<ref name="STAC">''[[Star Tours: The Adventures Continue]]''</ref> In addition, the Death Star superlaser's completion was delayed after a Rebel [[Mission to Desolation Station|attack]] on the Imperial facility of [[Desolation Station/Legends|Desolation Station]] resulted in the theft of the [[Tributary beam]] component as well as the total destruction of Desolation Station.<ref name="SWB:ES DS">''[[Star Wars Battlefront: Elite Squadron]]'' (DS version)</ref>

The [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] of the 501st Legion were among those assigned to protect the Death Star's interior. They were forced to put down a [[Death Star Uprising|prison break]] that had somehow occurred within the station, led by a Jedi [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] inmate. A number of prisoners were able to obtain a partial technical readout of the battlestation, which was beamed to a Rebel cell on [[Polis Massa/Legends|Polis Massa]]. Shortly after this embarrassing debacle, the 501st were reassigned and moved off the station.

Because of the controversial nature of its weaponry, Imperial officers were required by their [[Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide|field manual]] to refer to the Death Star concept in general or the DS-1 as the official title of Imperial Planetary Ore Extractor to any non-Imperial news outlets, as well as to report the questioner to the [[Imperial Security Bureau/Legends|Imperial Security Bureau]] for a thorough follow-up as a precaution.<ref name="Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide" />

====Battle of Horuz====
In 0 BBY the station [[Attack on the first Death Star|was attacked]] by a rebel force consisting of the [[Lucrehulk-class battleship/Legends|Lucrehulk-class battleship]] [[Fortressa]] and 500 [[X-wing starfighter/Legends|X-wings]]. The battle ended with the fleet being destroyed, and the Fortessa being struck by the Death Star's superlaser.<ref name="DSn" />

===The missing plans===
{{Main|Death Star plans/Legends}}
{{Quote|If the Rebels have obtained a complete technical readout of this station, it is possible, however unlikely, that they might find a weakness, and exploit it.''"<br />"''The plans you refer to will soon be back in our hands.|[[General/Legends|General]] [[Cassio Tagge/Legends|Cassio Tagge]] and [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]]|<ref name="ANH" />}}
The history regarding the acquisition of the [[Death Star plans/Legends|plans]] by the Rebel Alliance is a complex and convoluted one. Although three separate sets of schematics were stolen, only combined could they provide a thorough analysis of the space station's weaknesses.

====Learning the truth====
In [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]], [[Princess/Legends|Princess]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] of [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]], perhaps while the [[Alliance Intelligence/Legends|Alliance Intelligence]] investigated the existence of a superweapon, was informed about it by a soldier she rescued on [[Ralltiir/Legends|Ralltiir]]. The existence was justified by Intelligence on [[AX-235]]. [[Rianna Saren]]'s report on the [[Destruction of Despayre|Destruction]] of [[Despayre]] confirmed the power of the battlestation's superlaser.

In addition, [[Rahm Kota/Legends|Rahm Kota]] issued a [[Mission to Death Star I|reconnaissance mission]] to the station to gather intel on its primary systems, in particular its superlaser weapon. [[X2]] personally volunteered for the mission, feeling indebted to trying to stop the Empire he unwittingly aided in creating. At this time, the tributary beam had just been shipped to the Death Star, which X2 discovered via a transmission from X1 intended for the commander of the Death Star. X2, under Kota's command, then made an impromptu superlaser test on an ''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer that the Rebels had hijacked and scuttled earlier, causing them to realize the unimaginable destructive power behind the weapon.<ref name="SWB:ES PSP">''[[Star Wars Battlefront: Elite Squadron]]'' (PSP version)</ref>

Around the same time, Rebel leader [[Garm Bel Iblis/Legends|Garm Bel Iblis]], with help from professional thief [[Moranda Savich]], acquired a series of heavily encrypted [[Datacard/Legends|datacards]] from an Imperial defector on [[Darkknell/Legends|Darkknell]]. It was only after sending these to the Alliance that the resistance discovered the exact purpose of Governor Tarkin's "pet project": to inspire fear through the destruction of worlds.

====The combining of schematics====
{{Main|Operation Skyhook}}
{{Quote|Once it was finally finished, the Death Star was the Emperor's favorite toy.|[[Retired clone trooper]]|<ref name="BFII" />}}
Following the [[Death Star Uprising]], the aforementioned set of partial schematics was beamed to the Rebel base on Polis Massa. While it wasn't long before the Fighting 501st executed a [[Raid on Polis Massa|swift raid]] on the compound, [[Bothan/Legends|Bothan]] spies managed to transmit this first set off-base, presumably to their other asteroid base, AX-235. With one piece of the puzzle secure, the Alliance scrambled to secure more sets of plans, sets which would complete the picture.

[[File:LasercannonDSI.png|thumb|left|250px|Gun batteries attempt to defend against [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]].]]
It was at this time that a rumored Alliance cell on [[Kalakar Six]] had acquired the plans, and Palpatine and Vader investigated the matter personally. In the end, the effort was deemed a wild [[Bantha/Legends|bantha]] chase, as the planet was devoid of any Rebel sympathizers at all; in truth, the mission was most likely a ruse orchestrated by the Emperor to test his pupil's worth.

Meanwhile, real efforts to secure the Death Star plans were underway. Rebel agent [[Kyle Katarn]], a former [[Carida Academy/Legends|Imperial Academy]] graduate, had used his combination of stealth and brute force to wrest a supplemental set of plans from the Empire during the [[Mission to Danuta|Battle of Danuta]]. With two smaller examples of the schematics, the Rebels set about acquiring the last, largest set of plans.

Through the actions of operative [[Bria Tharen]] and [[Red Hand Squadron]], the Alliance engaged the enemy on the planet [[Toprawa/Legends|Toprawa]]. [[Operation Skyhook]], as it was called, resulted in one of the biggest victories to date for the Rebels: the final set of plans would at last be in their control.

On Toprawa, operative [[Havet Storm]] transmitted the plans, as well as the plans for the superlaser, to [[Tantive IV/Legends|''Tantive IV'']], a consular ship in orbit. With these two additional bits in tow, the [[Starship/Legends|starship]] fled the system and intercepted the readouts from Katarn and AX-235, with Princess Leia herself spearheading the entire operation. By taking advantage of her diplomatic immunity, Leia hoped to seek out [[Bail Prestor Organa/Legends|her father's]] friend, [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], and from there extrapolate a plan to analyze the schematics for a weakness in the superweapon's defenses.

But fate would take a different turn.

====The events above and on Tatooine====
{{Main|Battle of Tatooine (Galactic Civil War)}}
{{Quote|I have placed information vital to the survival of the Rebellion into the memory systems of this R2 unit. My father will know how to retrieve it.|Princess Leia refering to the Death Star plans|<ref name="ANH" />}}
[[File:DS_command_deck.png|thumb|right|200px|[[Grand Moff/Legends|Grand Moff]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin/Legends|Tarkin]] reviews the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|battle]] plan on the command deck of the Death Star.]]
When [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] and the 501st led a raid aboard ''Tantive IV'', no plans were to be found. At the last moment, Leia, realizing the importance of the plans' survival, placed them inside [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech droid]] [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]] who, alongside [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]], made their way down to the surface of [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] with the goal of delivering the plans for safekeeping to Obi-Wan. After being captured by scavenging [[Jawa/Legends|Jawas]] and then sold to [[Moisture farmer/Legends|moisture farmer]] [[Owen Lars/Legends|Owen Lars]], the astro-droid knew he was getting close to finding Kenobi. Accompanied by Owen's step-nephew, [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], R2 found who he was looking for.

===The Destruction of Alderaan===
{{Quote|You may fire when ready.|Grand Moff Tarkin|<ref name="ANH" />}}
After being captured by Lord Vader, Princess Leia was charged with espionage and [[Treason/Legends|treason]] and taken to the Death Star for interrogation, Vader's obsessive quest for the Rebellion's hidden base of operations being his primary focus. When she proved to be substantially resistant to Vader's methods of torture, Governor Tarkin ordered her to be brought to his command center. Tarkin threatened Leia with the destruction of her homeworld, [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]], and Leia deliberately misled him, saying that the Rebel base was on the remote planet of [[Dantooine/Legends|Dantooine]]. However, Tarkin, wanting a higher-profile target for his demonstration, ordered the [[Destruction of Alderaan/Legends|Destruction of Alderaan]] while Leia watched helplessly. Billions were killed; the overall effect of the operation was to spread the message of fear the Empire needed to keep all planetary systems under control.

===Battle of Yavin===
{{Main|Battle of Yavin/Legends}}
{{Quote|That's no moon. It's a space station.|Obi-Wan Kenobi, upon seeing the Death Star for the first time.|audio=ThatsNoMoon-ANH.flac|<ref name="ANH" />}}
Luke, Obi-Wan, [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]], [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]], C-3PO, and R2-D2, aboard the [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']], were captured in a [[Tractor beam/Legends|tractor beam]] after coming out of hyperspace near the remains of Alderaan and drawn onto the Death Star. They hid in several secret compartments in the ship while stormtroopers searched it, and then headed up to the control room. Obi-Wan devised a plan to free the ship by turning off a tractor beam projector.

[[File:Trench_Run_promo.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Rebel X-wings commence their attack run on the Death Star]]
After learning that the Princess was on board, Luke, Chewie, and Han headed to her cell block. They managed to free her despite being [[Rescue of Princess Leia/Legends|attacked]] by stormtroopers. They fled by jumping into a garbage chute, and despite being nearly crushed as the walls compacted, escaped after R2 shut them down. Heading back to the ''Falcon'', they spotted a company of stormtroopers. The troopers were distracted by the battle between Obi-Wan and Darth Vader, allowing them to make it to the ship and take off, headed for Yavin IV.

There, R2-D2 uploaded the data tapes, and Alliance tactician Jan Dodonna found a weakness in the station: an [[Deflector shield/Legends|unshielded]] thermal exhaust port that, if fired upon with a [[Proton torpedo/Legends|proton torpedo]], would set off a chain reaction and annihilate the battlestation.

The ensuing [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]] destroyed the Death Star, just as it was positioned to destroy the newly discovered Rebel Base on Yavin's fourth moon. The Death Star was destroyed by Luke Skywalker in the [[Trench Run Defense#The classic "trench run"|trench run]], who, with the help of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]], successfully fired two proton torpedoes into the exhaust shaft that led directly into the Death Star's main reactor. Yavin 4 would have been destroyed by the Death Star seconds earlier had it not been for the hesitations of [[Master chief petty officer|Master Chief Gunnery Officer]] [[Tenn Graneet]], who delayed the firing because of his regrets for destroying Alderaan even though he was loyal to the Empire. He told his crew to "Stand by," unknowingly buying the Rebel Alliance the time to successfully destroy the battlestation.<ref name="DSn" /> Ironically, shortly before Luke Skywalker fired the proton torpedoes into the thermal exhaust port, Palpatine had ordered the creation of a [[Death Star II/Legends|second Death Star]].<ref name="EGW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref>

[[File:Exds.png|thumb|right|250px|The Death Star is destroyed at [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin]]]]
The reactor exploded, destroying the battlestation and killing everyone still on board, including Grand Moff Tarkin. It would prove a decisive moment for the Rebellion, and gave young Skywalker his first spot in galactic history. Even though the Empire remained the most prominent military power in the galaxy, this major Alliance victory gained credibility and support for their movement. In the months following the battle, thousands of star systems joined the Alliance, leading to the escalation of the Galactic Civil War.

Although the destruction of the Death Star was primarily an Alliance victory, it also acted as a blessing in disguise for the Empire, in particular the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]]. Because its development diverted untold amounts of credits and talent from the Navy, other development projects, including those directly related to the creation of a new class of Star Dreadnoughts that would act as a new pinnacle of capital-ship power, experienced a lot of delays. The Death Star's destruction gave the project in question a newfound importance to the Empire.<ref name="EGW" />

In addition, extensive data had been beamed to a communications complex on [[Galvoni III]], which included a lot of transmissions, images, and footage of events up to the last seconds of the Death Star's existence, including the rescue of Organa and other related events. The Rebel Alliance&ndash;aligned historian [[Voren Na'al/Legends|Voren Na'al]] infiltrated the complex and stole much of this data, narrowly escaping and eventually publishing a report on the superweapon.<ref name="GG1">''[[Galaxy Guide 1: A New Hope]]''</ref><ref name="DSOTM" />

===Wreckage===
[[File:Bring_DS_debris.png|thumb|left|An Imperial officer brings a piece of debris from the Death Star for analysis.]]
Soon after the destruction of the giant battle station, salvaging companies and other organizations such as the [[Ugor/Legends|Ugors]]<ref name="Galaxy Guide 2">[[Galaxy Guide 2: Yavin and Bespin (Second Edition)|''Galaxy Guide 2: Yavin and Bespin'', Second Edition]]</ref> and the [[Ni'lyahin Smugglers]]<ref name="SonyCite-Star Chart: Yavin System">{{SonyCite|url=en_US/players/content.vm?id=66854&resource=features|text=Star Chart: Yavin System}}</ref> arrived at Yavin IV and carted off large chunks of debris. It didn't take long before the Empire stepped in and stopped all further theft by unauthorized agencies.<ref name="Galaxy Guide 2" />

The Empire set up an [[Imperial Salvage Station]] in orbit around Yavin IV to collect the floating remains of the destroyed Death Star. The salvage team aboard the station was led by [[Major/Legends|Major]] [[Reskik]] of the Imperial Security Bureau. The salvage teams consisted of civilian engineers sent by the major defense contractors that had provided the primary system designs for the Death Star project. Additional zero-G work crews were provided by the Empire.<ref name="Galaxy Guide 2" />

Countless pieces of debris rained down on the jungle moon. Many left scorched craters behind and set the jungles on fire. Some pieces remained largely intact. After the Alliance left Yavin 4, many salvage teams combed the jungles to recover pieces of Death Star technology. Many independent salvagers like [[Nagem Dr'Lar]] sold the debris to the Empire. But other organizations interested in the Empire's technology also sent their own teams to the remote moon. The [[Hutt Expeditionary Force]] led by [[Osae Meilea]] tried to recover debris for the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] crimelords. Even the [[Black Sun/Legends|Black Sun]] crime cartel tried to get their hands on pieces of the destroyed station.<ref name="galaxies">{{GalaxiesAED}}</ref>

A year after the Death Star's destruction, some spacers had a piece of wreckage from the battlestation.<ref name="galaxies" />

[[Tyber Zann]], Crime Lord of the [[Zann Consortium/Legends|Zann Consortium]], was interested in some of the Death Star's debris since it contained information about the [[Aggressor-class destroyer|''Aggressor''-class Star Destroyer]] and the [[Eclipse-class dreadnought|''Eclipse''-class Super Star Destroyer]].<ref name="eaw">''[[Star Wars: Empire at War: Forces of Corruption]]''</ref>

==Commanders and crew==
{{Expandsect}}
[[File:Deathstar-command.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Death Star command organization]]

Like any organization within the Galactic Empire, the command structure within the Death Star was very strict. Command sectors were found throughout the Death Star, and were supervised by Imperial officers with a rank of lieutenant or higher.

Excluding visitations from the Emperor, the battlestation fell under the direct command of a triumvirate headed by Grand Moff Tarkin, Admiral Conan Antonio Motti of the Imperial Navy, and High General Cassio Tagge of the Imperial Army. The Chiefs of Navy, Army, and Battle Station Operations were held by officers with the rank of Colonel, or, in the case of [[Trech Molock/Legends|Trech Molock]], High General. Below each Operations Chief were eight majors who served as chiefs of specific departments under heir branch of operations. Four majors were also responsible for the general, service, technical, security, and military sectors, the last of which included Army troopers, gunners, pilots, and specialized versions of the Navy Troopers known as the Death Star Troopers. Members of the Imperial Security Bureau (ISB) were also stationed on board.

There were also two significant portions of the Death Star's complement that did not fall under the normal command structure yet were notable. The first was the Emperor's emissary, Darth Vader, who answered to Tarkin and otherwise was not subject to any other authority aboard the battle station. The second were the Stormtrooper Corps. While the Stormtroopers could work alongside the Army and Navy troopers as well as the ISB personnel if their services were required, they did not fall under their jurisdiction and thus were hardly subservient to either branch, as their primary loyalty was to Emperor Palpatine alone. They also worked to ensure that all officers complied with the policies of the Emperor's New Order.

At any given time, around 1.7 million Imperial personnel (excluding [[Droid/Legends|droids]]) were aboard the battlestation.

===Security Sector===
The security sector was the sector of the Death Star charged with patrolling and guarding vital or off-limits areas aboard the Death Star. The members of the security sector were the Imperial security officers, otherwise known throughout the Empire as wardens. Their duties included, besides patrols and guarding vital or off-limit areas, the maintenance of detention cell blocks, policing corridors, and protecting visiting officials. The wardens were likewise among the only Imperial officers aboard the battle station to carry personal weapons at all times. The wardens were assigned to several different security divisions, including enforcement, protection, surveillance, and detention, the last three working together to create a complete umbrella of security aboard the battlestation. The surveillance stations remained on alert throughout all duty shifts, relying on a myriad of hidden cameras, sensors, mobile remotes, and droids. However, the wardens themselves were under constant surveillance and observation, due to each standard security sector being required to provide office space and reasonable assistance to the ISB. The ISB and the security forces maintained a tense relationship, largely because the ISB was well known for placing undercover agents among military and technical-support personnel as well as their policing and surveillance techniques being even harsher than regular Imperial security standards. They also maintained their own armory on each sector.

Members of the security sectors were also charged with putting down disturbances (such as an out-of-control argument between crew members) and restoring order, as the Death Star was comparable to a community by Tarkin, himself a former commander of the Republic Outland Regions Security Force.

===Service and Technical Sectors===
The Service and Technical Sectors were tasked with maintaining the Death Star. Technicians were assigned to these two sectors. The Service Sector was tasked with inspecting, maintaining, repairing, and replacing machinery. The jobs varied from highly skilled technicians trained to build components from scratch, to droids programmed to clean corridors. In addition, members of the Service Sector were required, as their most important duty, to keep up the station's protective and emergency gear. They were also required to maintain a variety of gear, from TIE Fighter pilot gear to Viper Probe Droids. RA-7 protocol droids worked throughout the station, including in the maintenance sections, which earned them the nickname of "Death Star Droids," despite technically being outnumbered by the MSE-6 droids. When not assigned to performing repairs or routine maintenance of the machinery aboard the station, the members of the Service Sector were stationed at monitoring posts to check temperature and performance readings or waited for system-failure alarms to sound from diagnostics systems built in to the Death Star's machinery. They also were assigned to clean carbon buildup, change components, and overhaul engines at shops. Technical Sector technicians&mdash;those not selected for the Service Sector&mdash;worked in the science stations, medical bays, research laboratories, programming facilities, and engineering stations, with the possibility of developing a weapon even more destructive than the superlaser. Members of this sector, however, were constantly reminded that while they were important due to their service to the Empire, specifically to the Death Star, they were not more important than the military sector. The staff assigned to the medical stations of this sector possessed varying ranks and abilities, although their droids specialized in various medical techniques, including surgery, anesthesia, and prosthetics.

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Deathstar_negwt.png|thumb|left|200px|The first Death Star]]
The [[West End Games]] roleplaying game claimed that the first Death Star had a diameter of 120 kilometers.

The fact book ''[[Star Wars: Incredible Cross-Sections]]'' and detailed scaling of the station in the film suggested that the Death Star actually was 160 kilometers in diameter. However, according to statements by [[Grant McCune]], Chief Model Maker for the movie,<ref>{{BanthaCite|issue=6|article=Questions & Answers}}</ref> the scale used for the Death Star in the film was 1:180,000. The Death Star model was 120 centimeters in diameter<ref name="BtM" /> which indicates that the Death Star was intended to be 216 kilometers in diameter.

The fact book ''[[Death Star Owner's Technical Manual]]'' revised the diameter of the Death Star to 120 km.<ref name="DSOTM" /> [[Leland Chee]] clarified on Twitter that this was an "un-retcon" that was based on evidence presented by the writers.<ref name="Twitter Leland">{{Twitter|username=HolocronKeeper|url=status/399054790107222016|name=[[Leland Chee]]|date=2013-11-08|quote=The book creators lobbied relentlessly and after careful deliberation we decided to reinstate the old stats.  Call it an unretcon.|archivedate=20190722073136}} {{C|In response to: "It seems that the Death Star manual uses the original 120/160 km diameters instead of 160/900. Is this an error or a retcon?"</ref>

The explanation that the plans represent an earlier version is invalid, since the original plan in [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Attack of the Clones'']] shows the "later" form.<ref name="AOTC" /> Despite the fact that ''Attack of the Clones'' shows the plans in the "northern" hemisphere, ''The Essential Guide to Warfare'' states that the superlaser was originally on the equatior before being moved to the northern hemisphere.<ref name="TEGTW" />

In the [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Revenge of the Sith'']] DVD commentary, [[George Lucas]] made a comment that the Death Star seen at the end was the same Death Star that is seen in ''A New Hope''. He explained that "union disputes and supply problems" delayed its completion. (Intriguingly, the lead characters in Kevin Smith's film ''Clerks'' speculate at some length about whether the Imperial workers were unionized or subcontractors. This may or may not be an in-joke by Lucas.) However, the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] novel ''[[Jedi Search]]'' introduced what is referred to as a "Death Star prototype", implying that it was built before the Death Star seen in ''A New Hope''. This was retconned in ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'', which states that the Death Star prototype was a testbed prototype for the superlaser to be installed on the Death Star seen in ''A New Hope'', and that the Death Star shown at the end of ''Revenge of the Sith'' is in fact the same Death Star that is seen in ''A New Hope''.

A [[Death Star (novel)|eponymous full-length novel]], written by Michael Reaves and Steve Perry, was released in October [[2007]], and completely explains the events in and around the Death Star, during its construction, deployment, and eventual destruction. In ''Death Star'' it is stated that a zone was one twenty fourth of a hemisphere,<ref name="DSn" /> but other sources instead say there was twenty four zones total.<ref name="TCSWE" /><ref name="TEGTW" /> This article assumes ''Death Star'' is in error for this point.

In a number of adventure paths the reader may take in the story of [[The Clone Wars: Decide Your Destiny: Tethan Battle Adventure|''Tethan Battle Adventure'']], [[Sue Behrent]]'s [[2010]] entry in the ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Decide Your Destiny]]'' series of choose-your-own-adventure books, the [[Unidentified Tethan youngling|protagonist]], a [[Tethan]] [[Youngling/Legends|youngling]], witnesses the plans for the Ultimate Weapon. Depending on the choices the reader then makes, the youngling can subsequenly relay that information to Obi-Wan Kenobi and potentially also [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]], who then plans to tell Mace Windu about it, as well.<ref name="Tethan">''[[The Clone Wars: Decide Your Destiny: Tethan Battle Adventure]]''</ref>

In many [[Star Wars video games|video game]]s, particularly the [[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron (video game)|''Rogue Squadron'']] trilogy, the player has to avoid many obstacles and make several turns when flying in the Death Star's trench run. The schematics/layout of the Death Star show no objects or turns in the trench, and the appearance of the trench in video games is deemed non-canon. For the first game, [[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron (video game)|''Star Wars: Rogue Squadron'']], released in [[1998]], the Battle of Yavin is a bonus mission, unlocked by achieving all gold medals in the campaign or via cheat codes. The Battle of Yavin in the sequel, ''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron II: Rogue Leader]]'', is the game's first campaign mission and thus part of the game's [[canon]] storyline. Additionally, the Death Star serves as a location for multiple Versus Modes in ''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron III: Rebel Strike]]''.

[[1993]]'s ''[[Star Wars: Rebel Assault]]'' put players in the role of [[Rookie One]], who destroys the Death Star in place of Luke Skywalker. This article follows the sequence of events shown in [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']].

In the [[2002]] [[LucasArts]] video game expansion ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds: Clone Campaigns]]'' the Death Star can be summoned for players by typing the code "that's no moon" in the game's chatbox. The superweapon has the most powerful attack in the game, but it is slow to recharge.<ref name="CC">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds: Clone Campaigns]]''</ref>

===Non-canon history===
{{Quote|The ability to destroy a planet is... actually pretty impressive, when you think about it.|Darth Vader|<ref name="LEGO Star Wars: The Dark Side">''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Dark Side]]''</ref>}}
[[File:JusticeStar.jpg|thumb|right|150px|The Justice Star]]
In the [[Canon|non-canon]] comic ''[[Star Wars Infinities: A New Hope]]'', the attack on the battlestation fails, and the Empire manages to drive away the Rebel forces. Five years later, the Death Star is renamed the "'''Justice Star'''" to mark the fifth anniversary of the Rebels' defeat and becomes a mobile seat of government for the newly restored [[Imperial Senate/Legends|Imperial Senate]].

The Justice Star traveled from one system to the next, effectively replacing [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] as the center of the Empire. In an impressive display of symbolism, the Justice Star was stationed in front of Coruscant's sun, to eclipse it and thus be seen as a shining symbol of a new source of light for the galaxy.

This symbol was short-lived, however, as [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]] and [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]] commandeered the Justice Star, and used it to attack the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Fleet]], also manipulating Wilhuff Tarkin (by that point an Admiral) into doing so via a Jedi mind trick. Once the fleet was destroyed, they sent the battle station crashing into Coruscant's surface, killing [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] and destroying the massive [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapon]].

===LEGO sets and Kenner playsets===
*The first Death Star was represented by [[Kenner Products]] in the 1970s as a series of playsets (including the [[Devastator/Legends|''Devastator'']], of which there is a unique model with red box) to be joined to build the space station.
*[[The LEGO Group]] produced two different sets (10188 in 2008 and 9676 in 2012). The first was the station divided into many rooms and no outer shell, each room a scene from ''A New Hope'' or ''Return of the Jedi''; the second was a small model separable into two pieces, with inside the bricks to build a [[TIE/IN interceptor/Legends|TIE/IN interceptor]] in miniature.
